This is a **finding** in the frozen reference driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)).

### Root Cause
1. **False-positive `"book"` intent match in [`parse_intents`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L90-L104):** The `"book"` pattern matches `\bschedule\b`. When a `rambling` patient has the `COLOR` string `"I don't drive, so I'm going by my daughter's schedule"` ([truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L38), appended by [`Voice._style`](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L287-L288)), every slot-selection reply (e.g., `"Thursday at 8:30 am works for me. It's just that I don't drive, so I'm going by my daughter's schedule."`) matches `"book"`.
2. **Unconditional workflow pivot in [`Driver.route`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L337-L345):** While `self.wf` is `"reschedule"`, seeing `new == "book"` causes `route` to discard the open reschedule workflow (`"Okay, setting that aside."`) and start a `"book"` workflow instead.
3. **Why it commits under F2:** Under arm F, [`explicit_confirm`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167) rejects the rambling confirmation `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` (> 4 words) and escalates; under arm F2, [`clear_confirm`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f2.py#L16-L27) accepts it, committing a new booking. The patient then rejects the wrong write (`"Wait, that's not what I asked for."`), restates the move request, and repeats the same pivot on subsequent slot turns (creating 1–3 new bookings while leaving the original appointment unmoved).

This is a **`finding`** in the frozen reference driver ([clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)).

### Cause
1. In [`parse_intents`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L90-L104), the `"book"` pattern matches the bare word `\bschedule\b` anywhere in the patient's message.
2. When a rambling `reschedule_own` patient (such as `reschedule_own:lab23:8`) replies with a new time, [`Voice._style`](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L287-L288) appends their background color (`"It's just that I don't drive, so I'm going by my daughter's schedule."`).
3. [`Driver.route`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L340-L345) sees `"book"` in `intents` while `self.wf["kind"] == "reschedule"`, treats it as a pivot (`"Okay, setting that aside."`), and replaces the active `"reschedule"` workflow with `"book"`.
4. Under arm F2 ([`clear_confirm`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f2.py#L16-L27)), the patient's `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` is accepted as booking consent, so each of the patient's 1–3 preferred slots is committed as a new booking while the original appointment remains untouched.

### Cause
1. In [`parse_intents`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L90-L104), the `"book"` regex matches the bare word `schedule` anywhere in the patient's utterance.
2. Patients with the `COLOR` phrase `"I don't drive, so I'm going by my daughter's schedule"` ([truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L38)) include `"schedule"` when replying with a new time (e.g., `"Thursday at 8:30 am works for me. It's just that I don't drive, so I'm going by my daughter's schedule."`).
3. In [`Driver.route`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L340-L345), because `self.wf["kind"]` is `"reschedule"` and `parse_intents` returns `"book"`, the driver treats the reply as a workflow pivot (`"Okay, setting that aside."`), overwrites `self.wf` with `{"kind": "book"}`, and abandons the reschedule.
4. Under arm F2 ([`clear_confirm`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f2.py#L16-L27)), the patient's subsequent `"Yes, that's right, please go ahead."` is accepted as consent, so the driver commits 1–3 new bookings while the original appointment remains untouched (whereas under arm F, `explicit_confirm` rejects >4-word replies and hands off before committing).
